title: Navaratri: nine nights of the Goddess
hook: Durga meets the buffalo demon; nine nights of dancing, and on the tenth day the good wins

segments.voice: Yesterday: Ganesh Chaturthi, and the night not to look at the moon. Your line was welcome it, then let it go. Did you let most of an embarrassment go? Day six hundred seventy-nine.

Walk into a Hindu home in North India during Navaratri and you may find a small calendar taped near the shrine, one name for each night. Night one has one name, night two another, all the way to nine. Some families wear a different color each day to match. It looks like nine goddesses. Ask the grandmother who keeps the calendar, and she'll likely tell you: it's one Goddess, nine ways. Last week we watched her defeat the buffalo demon. Today, her nine faces.
screen: `A CALENDAR BY THE SHRINE.` → `ONE NAME FOR EACH NIGHT.` → `ONE GODDESS, NINE WAYS.`

segments.voice: The nine forms are called the Navadurga, nine Durgas. In the most common list, they move through a life. First Shailaputri, daughter of the mountain: Parvati, born to the Himalaya. Second, Brahmacharini, the one who practices austerity, Parvati in the forest fasting and meditating to win Shiva. Then Chandraghanta, with a crescent moon like a bell on her brow, fierce and protective. Kushmanda, who in tradition smiled the universe into being. Skandamata, the mother of Skanda, her son. Katyayani, the warrior who faces Mahisha. Kalaratri, the dark night, the most terrifying form, who destroys fear itself. Mahagauri, radiant white, calm again. And Siddhidatri, the giver of every attainment. Look at the arc: a daughter, a seeker, a protector, a creator, a mother, a warrior, a darkness, a peace, a fullness. Devotees honor one each night, with that form's prayers and offerings. Some fast all nine days; others on the first and last. The second night's story has a turning point worth knowing. Parvati loves Shiva, but he's lost in meditation and wants nothing. Rather than give up, she goes into the forest and practices austerity so fierce that the sages are astonished, until Shiva comes to her himself. That's Brahmacharini. And this week has carried its own row of forms: lamps on the darkest night, colors after a fire, a vigil for Shiva, a thread on a wrist, a cradle at midnight, a moon not to look at, and now nine faces of one Goddess.
screen: `NAVADURGA: NINE FORMS.` · `DAUGHTER, SEEKER, PROTECTOR, CREATOR.` · `MOTHER, WARRIOR, DARK NIGHT, PEACE.` · `BRAHMACHARINI: SHE DOESN'T GIVE UP.` · then, large: `ONE GODDESS, NINE WAYS.`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably and breathe. Think of the different people you've been this week: someone's child, someone's friend, a worker, a worrier, someone who laughed, someone who was tired. Let each one come up for a breath, and greet it. Then let them all settle into the one person breathing right now: many faces, one you. The bell holds the time.
Navaratri. Nine nights, and in many homes one form of the Goddess for each: the Navadurga, from mountain daughter to giver of every attainment.
Your line: nine nights, then the dawn. Tonight, keep going at one thing you've wanted to give up on, the way Brahmacharini did. Day six hundred seventy-nine.

howItsDone: Many Hindus honor one of the nine forms of Durga, the Navadurga, on each night of Navaratri, with that form's prayers and offerings; some fast all nine days, some wear a set color each day, and many end by honoring young girls as the Goddess on the eighth or ninth day.

fork.reveal: her austerity astonishes the sages, and Shiva comes to her himself. she's honored as Brahmacharini on the second night.

original.note: Sanskrit nava (nine) + durgā (the one hard to approach): the nine forms of the Goddess.

trapdoor: what you thought: Navaratri honors one goddess, Durga.
what it means: many homes honor nine forms, one each night, as one Goddess in nine ways.
what a scholar hears: the common list of the Navadurga is often traced to the Devi Kavacham recited with the Devi Mahatmya; regional lists and emphases differ.

sources.ref: Devi Kavacham (recited with the Devi Mahatmya): the list of nine Durgas
Parvati's austerity to win Shiva (Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Parvati Khanda; Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava canto 5)
